description:
**Pattern source**: bd:JMAP-826m.4 fixed MemoryBackend::query_objects to actually apply the typed filter and sort. The sibling MemoryBackend::query_changes at crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/memory.rs (line ~720 post-fix) still has _filter and _sort underscored, mirroring the pre-fix query_objects shape.

**Trigger**: any /queryChanges call with a non-null filter or sort against MemoryBackend ignores both and reports created/updated/destroyed from the raw change log. RFC 8620 §5.6 expects /queryChanges to return only entries that satisfy the filter — clients using a filtered /query and then a /queryChanges from that queryState get an inconsistent view.

**Out of scope of bd:JMAP-826m.4**: that bead's title and description named only  and lines 566-614 specifically. This sibling bead captures the same vulnerability in the adjacent /queryChanges path.

**Fix shape**: mirror the bd:JMAP-826m.4 pattern. Type-identity serde roundtrip on the filter into MetadataFilterCondition; reuse  to apply it. Sort similarly via . The created/updated/destroyed arrays from get_metadata_changes are already pre-filtered when the backend overrides get_metadata_changes (which this one does), so the residual /queryChanges filter is mostly for the auxiliary sort/queryState consistency. The destroyed array semantics under filtering follow draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-01 §3.5 — clients that filter SHOULD reuse the same filter for /queryChanges as for /query.

**Doc disclosure**: crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/memory.rs module doc (the //! block at top) already has a 'Metadata-specific behaviour' bullet calling out the /queryChanges gap, added in bd:JMAP-826m.4. Remove that bullet when this bead lands.
title: MemoryBackend.query_changes ignores filter and sort, same shape as bd:JMAP-826m.4 query_objects
